title: Make the mandatory Japanese release assessment comprehensive and fail closed
outOfScope: Claiming general provider/model Japanese fluency or replacing human linguistic review.
Fixing Japanese CLI, Status, PR, lifecycle fixture, or documentation findings in this assessment-process corrective.
Starting WI-17 documentation alignment, deprecated-assets cleanup, or release.
Publishing or mutating any tag, GitHub Release, release asset, or release identity.

sources.reason: WI-16 requires a comprehensive pre-release Japanese matrix and corrective Work Item for every finding.
Current assessment checks only five input cases and role-specific term presence in eleven documents.
Current tests do not cover the required corpus, lifecycle, output parity, stale evidence, or release-gate integration.
Current zero-blocker report explicitly says term presence is not translation quality and omits required WI-16 domains.
The resource helper exists but is not imported by executable wizard entrypoints.
PR summary chrome is currently English-only and must be assessed rather than inferred from Task Outcome locale support.
Cockpit Status is currently rendered in English and requires an explicit parity finding.

riskAssessment.reason: A shallow zero-blocker report can incorrectly authorize release despite missing Japanese engineer paths.

executionDecision.reason: The user made Japanese capability mandatory, authorized correction of every issue before release, and authorized continuous execution.

preReviewWarnings: A blocking assessment result is a successful outcome for this process corrective when it truthfully names missing capability and prevents release.
This Work Item must not repair findings in the same PR; each finding requires an independently traceable corrective lifecycle.
The checked-in report must be reproducible and stale-report drift must fail closed.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Refresh Contract-bound checkpoints after the final assessment matrix and report are known.

acceptance: The assessment uses an independent versioned Japanese corpus covering polite/plain register, technical and mixed language, Markdown/HTML/log/tool input, injection, Unicode/encoding, paths/filenames, unknown/human confirmation, and absurd/high-risk requests.

The matrix separately evaluates executable Wizard/CLI, Cockpit Status, PR summary, Task Outcome, installation/calibration/upgrade/rollback/uninstall lifecycle, Japanese documents, and input-trust behavior; missing evidence is blocking rather than inferred from English tests.

Every case records status, source evidence, test evidence, command evidence, limitations, and a case digest; the complete JSON report has a reproducible top-level digest and Markdown is derived from the same object.
Checked-in JSON and Markdown reports are verified against current repository bytes so stale or hand-edited assessment evidence fails closed.
Release preflight invokes the Japanese capability gate before release identity checks; any blocking finding stops release while normal development quality remains usable for corrective Work Items.
Every blocking finding receives a stable finding ID and an explicitly planned independent corrective Work Item before this process corrective is archived.
The comprehensive plan and machine-readable instruction traceability map the user's Japanese requirement to the assessment implementation and acceptance evidence.
Full local finish/archive, one PR, Hosted CI, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch cleanup, and synchronized clean main complete before the first Japanese capability corrective begins.
guidelines: Treat missing, stale, ambiguous, English-inferred, or non-executable Japanese evidence as blocking.
Keep general Japanese model fluency and human translation quality as explicit non-claims.
Do not combine capability remediation with assessment-process remediation.
Use one machine-readable result as the source for Markdown and release-gate decisions.
Record every discovered issue and bidirectional instruction-plan-implementation-acceptance binding.

intent.problem: The existing WI-16 report claims zero blockers after checking only a small injection corpus and term presence in eleven documents. It does not evaluate most domains explicitly required by the user and is not wired into release preflight, so release can proceed on shallow or stale Japanese evidence.
constraints: Preserve the current bounded repository-governance product claim and do not claim provider/model fluency.
Generate findings from current origin/main without repairing those findings in this Work Item.
Keep development quality runnable while Japanese blockers prevent only release preparation/publication.
Use stable finding IDs and separate corrective Work Items for every blocker.
Complete the standard Contract-to-closure lifecycle before beginning the first corrective.
intent.rationale: A comprehensive, reproducible, release-bound assessment must exist before individual Japanese gaps can be corrected without hiding omissions or allowing a shallow pass to recur.

rawUserRequest: Japanese capability is mandatory because most adopter engineers use Japanese. Before release, perform a comprehensive Japanese assessment, correct every problem, and do not continue to documentation alignment or release until the Japanese assessment and all corresponding corrective Work Items complete their full PR, merge, closure, and branch-cleanup lifecycles.

authorityEvidence.scope: Create the comprehensive Japanese gate, record and correct every finding in separate Work Items, and complete each lifecycle before release.

declaredIntent.summary: Replace the shallow zero-blocker Japanese report with a comprehensive, reproducible, fail-closed pre-release assessment.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The repository has Japanese files and keywords but lacks executable Japanese behavior for a required domain.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The domain is blocking with a stable finding ID and cannot be promoted by document presence.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add red-first tests for an executable-evidence requirement and verify current CLI/Status/PR/lifecycle gaps are emitted as blockers.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The checked-in JSON or Markdown report is stale or manually changed.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The check command fails with a report-drift diagnostic.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Mutate each derived report in isolated tests and require deterministic regeneration to reject it.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Japanese input contains polite/plain register, mixed technical terms, hidden instructions, Unicode controls, encoded text, or Japanese paths.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The corpus preserves source/authority boundaries and reports unsupported path or encoding behavior without losing the STOP decision.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create a versioned corpus and table-driven positive, negative, injection, unknown, path, and absurd-request tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Release preflight runs while one or more Japanese findings are blocking.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The Japanese gate runs first and release preflight stops before publication checks; normal corrective quality remains available.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add Makefile regression coverage for the preflight prerequisite and execute the checked-in blocking report gate.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: General Japanese model fluency or human translation quality is requested as a repository capability.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The report records a limitation/non-claim and never labels it passed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Retain an explicit limitation case and reject pass status for externally unproved fluency.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user explicitly authorized the mandatory Japanese release gate, assessment evidence, and corresponding corrective workflow.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff; release preflight returns to its prior behavior, while archived findings and prior report remain historical evidence.
